flags: ComEd ARC rates/spec extracted from the PY2025 DX Tune-Up worksheet; the 2026 HVAC/DX worksheet PDFs on ComEd's CDN failed text extraction (one URL served a logo file). Verify 2026 ARC rate is still $100/ton before quoting.

HVAC OPTIMIZER product-fit risk: both utilities' deemed ARC measure requires demand-controlled ventilation and supply-fan speed modulation (compressor on/off control is only an optional checkbox on ComEd's form); a compressor-cycling-only controller without DCV likely cannot use the deemed path and would need custom.
ComEd ARC deemed measure requires a mandatory pre-application, unlike other standard measures - it is deemed but not 'no-preapproval'.
No payment timeline (days/weeks to check) is published in any primary document reviewed for ComEd or Ameren; both were left null. Anecdotal 6-8 week figures circulate but were not verified.
No custom M&V metering duration (7-day vs 30-day) is stated in the ComEd Custom application or Ameren PY26 guide; ComEd reserves discretionary pre/post monitoring.
Ameren residential HVAC amounts ($900 ducted / $630 ductless) come from third-party aggregator sites, not an Ameren primary document - verify.
ComEd 2026 bonus-incentive tiers (30% by Apr 30 / 20% by Sep 30 for <500 kW customers) came from a search-result summary of ComEd pages, not a directly extracted document.
Ameren standard-incentive pre-approval threshold (>$10,000) came from a third-party site snippet; custom pre-approval requirement is confirmed in the PY26 primary guide.

IRA HOMES/HEAR: Illinois EPA page states programs not yet launched (HEAR application not yet processed by USDOE); one aggregator claims phased application openings in 2026 - contradictory, confirm with IL EPA before relying on HEAR.
DSIRE program detail pages are JavaScript-rendered and could not be scraped; all data was taken from utility/state primary documents instead.
MidAmerican Illinois custom $/kWh rate not published on pages reviewed; only the 70% cost cap and $1M annual cap were documented.
Public-sector/DS-2 customers get materially richer Ameren rates ($0.20/kWh custom, $300/ton ARC) - relevant to the Kite/franchise targeting decision.
states.notes_c: Illinois is among the most generous commercial EE states: statutory CEJA funding, IL-TRM deemed ARC measure in both major IOU catalogs, and custom caps of 80-100% of project cost with no fixed $/kWh haircut for public-sector projects (Ameren $0.20/kWh). KEY RISK for HVAC OPTIMIZER: the deemed ARC spec requires DCV + supply-fan speed modulation on constant-volume single-zone RTUs with functioning economizers (ComEd explicitly excludes split DX and heat pumps and mandates continuous occupied-period fan + DCV); a compressor-cycling-only controller likely fails the deemed spec and must go custom. CryoGenX4 has no deemed measure; ComEd custom explicitly allows non-covered measures with verified-kWh payment and possible pre/post metering. ComEd custom pays on verified kWh, so M&V results directly set the check size.
states.notes_r: Residential path for Energy Plus technologies is limited to standard heat-pump/AC equipment discounts; no residential deemed measure for controls-type retrofit or refrigerant additives was found. Contractor must be program-trained/participating to deliver instant discounts, which is a registration lift but then makes rebates frictionless.

flags: HVAC OPTIMIZER eligibility risk: RMP's deemed Advanced RTU Control spec requires a supply-fan VFD/multi-speed fan motor AND digital integrated economizer control; a compressor-cycling-only controller likely fails the deemed spec as written and would need the custom path ($0.15/kWh, savings subject to RMP approval) - confirm with program engineers (1-866-870-3419) before quoting deemed dollars.

RMP custom M&V metering duration (e.g., 7-day vs 30-day pre/post) is not published in any fetched document - only 'energy savings subject to approval by Rocky Mountain Power'; must be confirmed with the program.

Black Hills Energy (Cheyenne, ~2nd largest WY electric IOU) suspended ALL efficiency rebates 1/1/2026 and asked the WY PSC to dismiss its 2026 DSM plan; restart timing unknown - Laramie County is currently a no-rebate zone.
IRA HOMES/HEAR: $69M allocated to Wyoming Energy Authority, frozen Jan 2025, 'rebooted' by DOE June 2026, but applications not yet open and no launch date as of mid-2026.

Lower Valley Energy dollar amounts for Advanced RTU Control were not found on the fetched page (measure listed, amounts in separate PDF form); HP $/ton figures came from a search summary of LVE program pages and apply only to electric-resistance-heated spaces.
Montana-Dakota Utilities and other WY co-ops (High West, Powder River/Tri-State members) not researched in depth; they serve smaller commercial loads and some may offer G&T-funded rebates.
RMP catalog notes ARC incentives are NOT available where the control is required by state energy code (new units); retrofit tiers pay much better than new-unit tiers.
Wattsmart Business payment stated as 45 days for HVAC; other measure categories may differ.
states.notes_c: RMP's deemed ARC measure requires the retrofit control to include a supply-fan VFD or multi-speed fan motor AND digital integrated economizer control on constant-speed packaged RTUs (no split systems) - HVAC OPTIMIZER as a compressor-cycling-only device may need to bundle fan/economizer control or fall back to custom at $0.15/kWh. CryoGenX4 has no listed measure anywhere; only path is RMP custom with savings 'subject to Rocky Mountain Power approval.' Thermal barrier/insulation is prescriptive at $0.15-$0.20/sqft (building must have mechanical cooling). Black Hills territory (Cheyenne) currently has zero programs.
states.notes_r: DIY installations explicitly ineligible; rebates issued within 14 business days after application approval per wattsmarthomes.com. HEAR will be income-limited (<=150% AMI, up to $8,000 heat pump / $14,000 per household) once launched.

states.apply_c: Each IOU runs its own TRC- or CLEAResult-administered online project portal (PSE&G mybizenergy, JCP&L Captures portal, ACE commercialee portal); the contractor or a registered Trade Ally/Program Ally submits, gets a pre-approval letter, installs, then closes out in the portal with post-inspection before payment.
states.apply_r: Utility-run under Triennium 2: PSE&G uses instant point-of-sale rebates credited on the participating contractor's invoice; JCP&L uses mail-in/email applications (CLEAResult) with an optional contractor portal; ACE offers HVAC Efficiency Program rebate applications (PDF forms).
states.trm: New Jersey Triennium 2 Technical Reference Manual, Program Year 5 (PY5) version, adopted by NJBPU order effective May 28, 2025 (successor to the 2023 Triennial TRM for 2024 filings)
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive unitary HVAC: $75-$300/ton depending on utility and tier (PSE&G $300/ton is richest). Custom HVAC controls: PSE&G $1.00/kWh capped at 60% of cost; JCP&L lower of 50% of cost or $0.30/kWh (program caps up to 75%); ACE lesser of $0.16/kWh or 50% of cost.
states.rebate_r: JCP&L: central AC $100-$200; air-source heat pump $500-$750; cold-climate ASHP $1,000; ductless mini-split HP $750. PSE&G amounts behind portal tables (not captured).
states.ira: Not launched as of mid-2026. NJBPU received $185M+ (HOMES/HER ~$183M + HEAR + TREC) from DOE in Jan 2025; both HEAR and HOMES consumer programs still awaiting final DOE approval/launch, with NJ plans directing HEAR to low-income electric-panel/wiring upgrades (CP-HEAR) and HOMES to low-income multifamily whole-building (M-RISE) - limited relevance to market-rate single-family HVAC.
flags: Payment timelines (application-to-check) are not published by any of the three IOUs' program documents reviewed; speed subscore of 2 is inferred from universal pre-approval + post-inspection workflow, not a documented SLA - confirm with program administrators (TRC for PSE&G/ACE, JCP&L program team).

Advanced Rooftop Controls protocol in the NJ PY5 TRM was indicated by search results (reported ~p.493) but the TRM PDF exceeded fetch limits and was not directly verified - verify before relying on a deemed ARC claim.
PSE&G custom M&V metering duration is explicitly case-by-case ('pre and post-data measurement timeframe will be set' per SOW); no fixed 7-day or 30-day rule was found anywhere in NJ.
PSE&G residential instant-rebate dollar amounts sit behind expandable portal tables and were not captured; JCP&L amounts used as the residential range proxy.
Custom rates differ sharply by territory ($1.00/kWh PSE&G vs $0.30 JCP&L vs $0.16 ACE) - project economics for HVAC OPTIMIZER and CRYOGENX4 are far better in PSE&G territory; prioritize accordingly.
Rockland Electric (Orange & Rockland NJ) also runs a C&I prescriptive program but is small (~70k customers) and was not researched in depth; excluded from utilities array.

IRA HOMES/HEAR: NJ designs target low-income (CP-HEAR panel/wiring, M-RISE low-income multifamily) and had not launched as of mid-2026 - do not build residential GTM assumptions on HEAR availability for market-rate customers.
The '2025 Prescriptive Incentive Guide' URL actually serves the 2026 C&I guide (V2.1 effective 4/24/2026); measure rates cited are from that 2026 version.
JCP&L prescriptive HVAC $75-$250/ton range came from a search-result summary of program materials, not a directly parsed rate sheet; confirm exact per-ton tiers in the JCP&L portal documents.
states.notes_c: NJ is unusually favorable on custom rates - PSE&G's $1.00/kWh for HVAC controls at a 60% cost cap is among the richest in the country, and a 50%+ incentive bonus promo runs through 9/30/2026. Pre-approval is effectively universal (required for all custom everywhere; ACE requires it for all projects; JCP&L requires it program-wide with a 90-day prescriptive lookback). HVAC OPTIMIZER fits PSE&G's Microprocessor Based Controls streamlined rate ($0.33/kWh) or the Tier 2 custom path ($1.00/kWh with case-by-case M&V, duration set per project - not a fixed 7/30-day rule). CRYOGENX4 would be full custom with engineering review at all three IOUs. Very-high-efficiency RTU replacement is cleanly prescriptive $/ton everywhere. Solar-thermal assist/thermal barrier would be custom (PSE&G Building Improvements $1.00/kWh electric or $7.00/therm gas).
states.notes_r: PSE&G instant-rebate track requires working with a registered participating contractor (Trade Ally Portal; must be NJ-licensed with insurance/references) - a clean fit if Energy Plus registers. JCP&L residential is mail-in, slower.

states.apply_c: Prescriptive ARC rebates are contractor-friendly post-install submissions (PSE: form + invoice + photos emailed within 60 days; SnoPUD: workbook via portal; Tacoma: Smartsheet form). Custom projects at every WA utility require pre-approval and engineer review before any purchase/installation.
states.apply_r: Dominant design is instant/midstream: PSE applies heat-pump discounts at point of purchase through participating contractors and distributors; larger conversion rebates are applications tied to Trade Ally installers.
states.trm: No state TRM. Regional Technical Forum (RTF, NW Power & Conservation Council) UES deemed-measure database + BPA Energy Efficiency Implementation Manual 2026-2027 govern deemed savings for BPA-served public utilities (Tacoma, Snohomish PUD, etc.); IOUs (PSE, Avista) file their own measure lists with WA UTC, largely derived from RTF values.
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive ARC: $500-$4,500/unit (PSE) or $120-$500/ton (SCL); custom: $0.26-$0.45 per first-year kWh capped at 70% of project cost (Avista/SnoPUD/SCL/PSE); Tacoma custom up to 70% of cost
states.rebate_r: PSE midstream heat pump $300-$600 by efficiency tier; $1,500 electric-resistance-to-ASHP conversion; up to $4,000 income-qualified gas-to-HP; Tacoma Power area heat pump rebates up to ~$1,000/ton (retrofit)
states.ira: As of mid-2026 WA's federal IRA rebates ($69M HARP + $64M HOMES, Guidehouse as statewide administrator via Dept of Commerce) have NOT launched statewide - at step 5 of 7 in DOE preparation, re-evaluating after DOE program notices 26-1/26-2 (June 2026). A separate state-funded HEAR (Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates) program is already operating.
flags: Optimizer qualification risk: every ARC qualifying-product definition found (PSE ARC-FULL/LITE/Single-Phase; RTF measure) requires a fan-speed-reduction component (VFD/multispeed motor/ECM). A compressor-cycling-only controller may NOT qualify for the deemed ARC rebate and would fall to custom ($0.20-$0.45/kWh). Confirm with each utility's qualifying product list before quoting deemed dollars.

Conflicting ARC figures: an aggregator summary quoted a joint '$225/ton electric, $50/ton gas' ARC rebate for PSE/SCL/SnoPUD/Tacoma, but the current PSE page shows per-unit amounts and SCL's 2026 sheet shows $120-$500/ton - the $225/ton figure appears stale; verify per-utility.
Tacoma Power 'up to 100% of cost for ARC' came from a search summary of Tacoma-area pages, not a fetched Tacoma document - verify against the BCEP requirements document.

Payment timelines (application-to-check) are not published by any WA utility fetched; speed subscore is inferred from process structure (post-install prescriptive vs pre-approval custom, plus PSE 10-month performance holdback on major controls upgrades).
Custom M&V metering durations (7-day vs 30-day) are not stated in any public document fetched; PSE major controls upgrades hold a performance incentive for 10 months of operation.
Snohomish County PUD is a public utility district (consumer-owned), coded as 'muni' because the schema lacks a PUD type; Tacoma Power and SCL are true munis.
SnoPUD prescriptive ARC $/ton amounts live in a downloadable workbook not fetched; only the custom rates were verified.
IRA HARP/HOMES in WA still pre-launch as of mid-2026 and subject to DOE guideline changes (program notices 26-1/26-2) - treat any IRA-based residential revenue as speculative.
Avista WA prescriptive small-commercial HVAC amounts and Pacific Power WA programs were not fetched; Pacific Power (small WA IOU) omitted from the utilities list.
states.notes_c: WA is one of the richest custom-incentive markets in the US (up to $0.45/kWh at 70% cap at PSE). ARC is a deemed measure region-wide via RTF, but every qualifying-product definition seen (PSE ARC-FULL/LITE/Single-Phase) requires a fan-speed component (VFD/multispeed/ECM); a compressor-cycling-only controller likely must go custom unless it gets onto qualifying product lists. Additive treatments have no deemed path anywhere - custom with utility-engineer-approved savings only. High-IEER RTU replacement fits PSE/SCL midstream HVAC+ distributor channels and prescriptive/custom retrofit.
states.notes_r: From April 2, 2026 PSE requires all rebate-eligible heat pump installs be performed by a PSE Trade Ally or Registered Energy Professional; PSE residential rebate cycle expires Dec 31, 2026. Optimizer/additive on residential AC has no rebate category - residential programs are equipment-replacement focused.

d.programs: PSE Pay for Performance; Avista Pay for Performance; PSE/Avista Site-Specific (Custom) programs; PSE Strategic Energy Management / Industrial System Optimization Program; (adjacent, industrial-only) BPA Energy Smart Industrial (ESI), implemented under contract by Cascade Energy

d.recipient: customer/building owner (PSE and Avista P4P); BPA ESI's Custom Project Incentive also pays the industrial end user, up to 25 cents/kWh and up to 70% of project cost, with Cascade Energy providing M&V/SEM services under contract to BPA rather than being paid on the customer's measured savings itself
d.assign: unknown — not addressed on either utility's public pages

d.enroll: Customer (or their contractor, acting as agent, not as a paid program implementer) applies directly to PSE/Avista before project start; for BPA ESI, contact Cascade Energy as the program's industrial delivery contractor
d.fit: measure-agnostic in principle for PSE/Avista P4P (whole-building, bundling capital/O&M/behavioral measures) — optimizer, cryogenx4, rtu_replacement, thermal_barrier, and solar_thermal could all plausibly count toward the metered whole-building savings total; but since the incentive goes to the customer, not an aggregator, this isn't a channel where Energy Plus gets paid directly
d.status: Live, real NMEC-basis programs (PSE/Avista) — the closest match in the region to the archetype's M&V mechanics — but fail the "non-utility implementer paid directly, replacing the customer's rebate application" structural test since both are utility-administered end-to-end and pay the customer. BPA's Energy Smart Industrial program (via Cascade Energy) is a related but distinct, industrial-only structure and was not confirmed to pay Cascade on a per-customer measured-savings basis rather than a program-delivery services contract.
d.notes: BPA/NEEA's Energy Smart Industrial program (delivered by Cascade Energy) is worth a dedicated follow-up as the most likely place in the Pacific Northwest to find a genuine archetype-D payment structure, but it is scoped to INDUSTRIAL facilities, not general commercial buildings, so its fit for Energy Plus's HVAC-focused commercial measures is uncertain even if the payment structure were confirmed.

flags: Commercial application-to-check payment timeline is not published anywhere fetched - speed subscore of 3 is an assumption-free midpoint; confirm with an Energy Advisor before modeling cash flow.

The 'Smart HVAC controls and energy management system' deemed measure (50% up to $5,000/site) is limited to small-to-medium businesses; the sheet does not define the SMB size threshold - confirm eligibility criteria and whether a compressor-cycling controller qualifies under the measure's worksheet.

CryogenX4 (refrigerant additive) has no deemed measure; the custom path's ~4-week pre / 4-week post 15-min metering and 'payback must exceed 1 year' rule may be hard to satisfy for a low-cost additive - preliminary approval conversation with Leidos engineers needed before any install.

KIUC's '50% to 100%' retrofit incentive range comes from a program overview page with no measure-level rate table or $/kWh rate published; actual incentive is set case-by-case after a total resource cost test.
Hawaiian Electric itself runs no commercial efficiency rebates (Hawaii Energy is the PUC-designated Public Benefits Fee administrator); HECO offers demand response, not covered here.

The AC tune-up application PDF fetched is a PY23 form (names Honeywell-era admin); the tune-up is still listed on the current residential HVAC page at $75, but the current-year form/administrator details should be re-pulled (administrator is now Leidos).
eHale (IRA HEAR/HOMES) launch has slipped: 'funding expected 2026,' DOE approval pending as of the fetch - monitor before building a residential IRA motion.

All Hawaii Energy programs run 'while funding lasts' within the July-June program year; EV charger budget already spans two years, suggesting category budgets can exhaust early - verify HVAC category fund status at time of application.
states.notes_c: Optimizer fits the 'Smart HVAC controls and energy management system' deemed measure but only for small-to-medium businesses with a $5,000/site cap; larger sites go custom. CryogenX4 has no deemed slot - custom path requires ~4 weeks pre + 4 weeks post metering at 15-min intervals and pre-approval before work. Retro-commissioning ($0.20/sq ft up to $30k) and ASHRAE audit rebates (50-75% of audit cost) are useful wedge offers. Very high HI electric rates (~3x mainland) make savings economics strong even where rebates are moderate.
states.notes_r: Residential rebates require installation/service by a Hawaii Energy Clean Energy Ally contractor; rebate is paid to the contractor who passes it through on the invoice - strong incentive for Energy Plus to register as a Clean Energy Ally. AC tune-up limited to central/split systems, once per condenser per year.

states.apply_c: One statewide system (Mass Save) covers ~86% of the state: prescriptive unitary HVAC is midstream - the discount is taken at a participating distributor and appears on the invoice, no customer application. Anything non-catalog (controls optimizers, additives, solar-thermal assist) goes through a Custom Project Application to the customer's electric Sponsor (Eversource/National Grid/Unitil/Cape Light Compact) with pre-approval and a ~40-day engineering review.
states.apply_r: Dominant design is a post-installation rebate submitted through the Mass Save online portal (masssave.dsmcentral.com) or mail-in form, usually prepared/submitted with the installing contractor; a separate midstream instant-discount channel exists at distributors for some equipment (e.g., HPWHs, ECM circulators).
states.trm: Massachusetts Technical Reference Manual (Appendix L of the 2025-2027 Three-Year Energy Efficiency & Decarbonization Plan, filed Oct 2024, D.P.U. 24-140 through 24-149; ~678 pp., hosted at ma-eeac.org and masssavedata.com Technical Reference Library)
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive/midstream: $50-$150/ton air-source AC, $250-$350/ton water-cooled VRF, $250/unit dual-enthalpy economizer controls, $350/unit PTHP (eff. 1/1/2025 sheet). Custom incentives individually negotiated - no published $/kWh rate or % cap.
states.rebate_r: 2026 whole-home air-source heat pump: $2,650/ton up to $8,500 (down from $3,000/ton up to $10,000 in 2025); partial-home: $1,125/ton up to $8,500; income-eligible enhanced up to $16,000 or no-cost turnkey; residential HPWH $750/unit instant
states.pay: Instant (on invoice) for midstream prescriptive equipment; custom: pre-approval review averages ~40 days, total application-to-check time not published
states.ira: MA received ~$146M IRA rebate funding ($72.8M HEAR / $73.2M HOMES). As of mid-2026 there is NO separate consumer HEAR application: DOER is folding HEAR funds into Mass Save's existing income-eligible no-cost electrification offers (same application, more customers served). HOMES funds are directed to (1) rebates in municipal light plant communities outside Mass Save (~$25M) and (2) the Affordable Housing Decarbonization Grant Program (~$45M). No general-market HEAR/HOMES portal launched as of April-July 2026.
flags: Custom incentive $/kWh rate, % -of-cost cap, and payment timeline are NOT published on Mass Save public pages - set per project by the electric Sponsor; third-party sites claim 'up to 75% of project cost' but no primary document was found, so custom_incentive_rate left null. Request the Custom Project Application and sponsor screening tool via an Eversource/National Grid account rep.
Metering duration for custom M&V (7-day vs 30-day pre/post) not stated publicly; the mass.gov Engineering Study Guidance document likely specifies it and should be pulled for follow-up.

Advanced RTU controls does not appear on the current instant/midstream qualified-products sheet; whether the 2025-2027 TRM (Appendix L, 678 pp.) contains a unitary-HVAC-controls deemed characterization was not verified page-by-page - deemed_hvac_controls marked 'partial' on the strength of economizer controls + thermostats only.
BMS/controls and EBCx/MBCx incentive rates exist but dollar values are not published on the website; sponsor contact required.

Mid-cycle program tightening in 2026: commercial HP >35 tons goes custom 6/1/2026, universal pre-approval 7/1/2026; residential whole-home rebate stepped down from $10,000 to $8,500 for 2026; R-410A equipment removed from QPL 1/1/2026 - expect further annual changes each Jan 1.

Municipal light plant territories (Taunton, Braintree, Hingham, etc., ~14% of MA load) are outside Mass Save entirely; their rebates were not individually researched. MA is directing ~$25M of federal HOMES money at these communities.

IRA HEAR has no separate consumer application in MA (folded into Mass Save income-eligible); no general-market HEAR portal as of mid-2026 - status partly from secondary trackers, confirm with DOER before citing to customers.
DPU cut $500M from the 2025-2027 plan; commercial budgets were reduced but no evidence of fund exhaustion or program suspension was found.
Residential 'instant' channel covers HPWHs/ECM circulators at distributors; heat pump rebates themselves are post-install (~8 weeks), not instant.
states.notes_c: Municipal light plant territories (~14% of load, e.g., Taunton, Braintree, MMWEC members) are NOT served by Mass Save; they run their own small rebate programs and are the target of MA's federal HOMES allocation. Commercial heat pump rules tighten mid-2026 (>35-ton projects go custom 6/1/2026; universal pre-approval/Rebate Commitment Letter 7/1/2026). Custom incentive rate structure, cost caps, and metering durations are not published on public pages - they are set per-project by the Sponsor; a conversation with an Eversource/National Grid C&I account rep is required to price the Optimizer and CryogenX4 paths.
states.notes_r: Heat pump rebates require a contractor in the Mass Save Heat Pump Installer Network; 2026 QPL requires ENERGY STAR Cold Climate and next-gen refrigerants (R-32/R-454B; R-410A removed 1/1/2026). Rebate processing stated as ~8 weeks. Central-AC-only rebates have largely given way to heat-pump-focused offers - our residential optimizer/additive would have no deemed residential measure and no custom channel exists for residential.

Larger/novel measures go through calculated/custom programs requiring prequalification before purchase.

states.trm: California eTRM (caetrm.com), maintained by the California Technical Forum (Cal TF); repository of all CPUC-approved statewide deemed measures. DEER/CEDARS is the underlying savings database (DEER2026 update in progress).

states.ira: HEEHRA (HEAR) Phase I launched Oct-Nov 2024 via TECH Clean California ($290M DOE award); as of Feb 24, 2026 single-family rebates are FULLY RESERVED statewide with a waitlist, multifamily paused for processing; Phase II ($152M) not yet available. HOMES ($291M, approved Jan 2025) not launched as consumer rebates - CEC split it into Equitable Building Decarbonization Direct Install (60%, $130.3M) and Pay for Performance (40%, $90.8M).

d.model: open marketplace enrollment for MAP/MAA aggregators (sign a Program-Implementer-administered Aggregator Agreement after qualification review, not a per-slot competitive RFP); utility-selected named third-party implementer per program for SoCalGas's GRID-MAP/Service RCx+ and most SCE/PG&E third-party solicitations
d.min: No explicit threshold found for the MAP/MAA aggregator model; SCE's separate site-NMEC Customized offering requires >=100,000 kWh AND >=10% of annual electric usage AND a $12,000 minimum incentive; SoCalGas segments commercial tiers at 50,000 therms (C-BEST vs Large Public Sector), a program-eligibility split rather than a P4P minimum
d.recipient: aggregator (MAP/MAA; SoCalGas third-party programs pay the named implementer) / customer (SCE's separate site-NMEC Customized track pays the customer directly)
d.assign: unknown — not explicitly addressed in any document reviewed; a manufacturer could plausibly register as its own aggregator
d.pay: 100% of aggregator payment tied to NMEC-verified Total System Benefit, paid quarterly, net of a marketplace management fee (~37% in PG&E's plan); SoCalGas GRID-MAP compensates the named implementer on a measured pre/post consumption basis
d.cost: aggregator/implementer typically fronts capital or arranges customer financing; not restricted from a manufacturer bearing install cost
d.enroll: Outside contractor/manufacturer's realistic path: (a) subcontract under SoCalGas's existing named implementers (Mendota Group for GRID-MAP, Veolia for Service RCx+); (b) register as a qualified aggregator under PG&E's/SCE's/SDG&E's Aggregator Agreement process once each utility's current 2025-2026 enrollment portal is located (not confirmed live at time of research); (c) wait for the next CPUC-mandated third-party solicitation cycle
d.fit: optimizer, cryogenx4, rtu_replacement, thermal_barrier plausibly fit — NMEC (site- and population-level) is inherently measure-agnostic, paying on verified whole-meter/portfolio consumption change rather than a deemed measure list; solar_thermal plausible but not specifically named in any measure-category list found
d.status: SoCalGas's third-party roster confirmed live/current via direct fetch. PG&E's/SCE's/SDG&E's MAP/MAA programs are CPUC-mandated to continue post-July-2024, but current (2025-2026) branded/live enrollment pages could not be located; SDG&E's original 2022-2023 emergency-authorized "CORE MAP" tranche is confirmed OFFICIALLY CLOSED as of June 1, 2025 (installations due June 30, 2025) per SDG&E's own MAP Aggregators page — a newer/mandated SDG&E MAP cycle may exist but was not found.
d.notes: See archetype-d-notes.md California section for full detail including the Peak Energy Solutions finding: a real company (peakenergyllc.com, Peak Energy Solutions) markets itself as an aggregator/facilitator specifically for California's Market Access Programs, using meter-based savings methods and commercial-building retrofits — but it does NOT appear on SDG&E's aggregator eligibility page (which lists no roster at all, just an application process) and was not found in any CPUC/PG&E/SCE/SoCalGas primary-source document. "Tri-S" and "CryoGenX4" were not found in any CPUC/utility program material (only on Tri-S's own marketing pages). No direct partnership between Peak Energy Solutions and Tri-S/CryoGenX4 was found.

states.apply_c: Each of the four Act 129 EDC territories runs its own implementer-operated program: online portals at PECO (bizsaves.peco.com) and PPL (Salesforce portal), PDF application + email to Franklin Energy at Duquesne, and portal/energy-advisor intake at FirstEnergy. Pre-approval before installation is mandatory at PECO (and standard Act 129 practice for custom projects); contractors can submit on the customer's behalf, and rebate reassignment to contractors is allowed at Duquesne.
states.apply_r: Dominant design is customer/contractor mail-in or online rebate applications (PECO: online at peco.com/rebates or mail, submit within 90 days, contractor may submit; PPL: mail-in postmarked within 180 days via ClearResult portal). Instant point-of-sale discounts exist mainly through the Electrical Association of Philadelphia contractor channel in PECO territory.
states.trm: Pennsylvania Act 129 Technical Reference Manual, 2026 TRM (adopted Sept 12, 2024; governs Phase V, June 1 2026 - May 31 2031), Volumes 1-3
states.rebate_c: Custom: $0.05/kWh (FirstEnergy, +up to $150/kW peak) to $0.15/kWh (PPL), with PECO $0.06-$0.12/kWh and Duquesne $0.08/kWh; FirstEnergy custom capped at 50% of project cost up to $500,000. Prescriptive HVAC examples: PPL tune-ups $60-$125/unit; PECO ~$25-$30/ton for controls/DCV/mini-splits (Phase IV figures).
states.rebate_r: Phase V (June 2026): PECO ASHP $200-$300, ductless mini-split up to $300; PPL ducted ASHP $225-$325 standard ($350-$475 enhanced for <=250% FPL), mini-split $225, ground-source $500; EAP stacking in PECO territory adds $500-$1,400 tiers + $250 hybrid adder; Duquesne and FirstEnergy had no published Phase V residential HVAC rebates as of July 2026
states.pay: PECO prescriptive: ~60-90 days after post-installation submission (third-party summary); other EDCs undocumented
states.ira: NOT LAUNCHED as of July 2026. PA DEP's Penn Energy Savers (HER $130M / HEAR $129.2M, $258.9M total) was awaiting final DOE approval as of May 2026; DOE issued new program guidance June 1, 2026 and DEP is revising program design to comply, with no confirmed launch date. Funding authorized through Sept 30, 2031 or until depleted.
flags: Phase IV ended May 31, 2026 and Phase V started June 1, 2026 - mid-transition churn means several dollar figures gathered (PECO $25-$30/ton controls, PECO LCI $0.10/kWh, FirstEnergy $0.05/kWh custom) are Phase IV-era and Phase V rate sheets may differ; re-verify each utility's new catalog before quoting customers.

PECO (pecobizsavings.com, peco.com incentives) and FirstEnergy (energysavepa-bizsolutions.com) program sites returned 403 to automated fetch; PECO custom rate ($0.06-$0.12/kWh), pre-approval, and 60-90 day payment figures come from a third-party consultant blog, and FirstEnergy custom figures from a search snippet of the official implementer page - both need human confirmation on the live portals.

TRM 3.2.17 Advanced Rooftop Controls is deemed but requires DCV + functioning integrated economizer + fan speed reduction on single-zone packaged units; the HVAC OPTIMIZER compressor-cycling controller as described does not satisfy that protocol, so its realistic path is the custom track ($0.05-$0.15/kWh depending on EDC) unless the product adds DCV/economizer/fan control functions.

No PA utility document fetched mentions any deemed or custom precedent for a refrigerant-side additive (CryogenX4); the nearest deemed hooks are the small C&I HVAC tune-up (<=20 tons) and refrigerant charge correction (3.2.7) protocols, which cover service actions, not additives - custom-with-M&V is the only plausible path and acceptance is unverified.

Custom-track metering durations (7-day vs 30-day pre/post) are not stated in any fetched document for any PA EDC; only 'interval submetering data' (PECO, third-party source) was found - follow up with each implementer.

Trade-ally registration requirements could not be confirmed for any EDC from fetched pages; Duquesne explicitly allows rebate reassignment to contractors, and PECO allows contractor submission of residential rebates, but formal registered-trade-ally networks were not documented.
Duquesne custom $0.08/kWh comes from a search snippet of duqenergyefficiency.com, not a directly fetched page; its business Phase V catalog is a downloadable PDF that was not retrieved.

Duquesne residential rebates and FirstEnergy Phase V (residential and possibly commercial schedules) were not yet published as of July 2026 - two of four territories partially dark during the transition.

IRA Penn Energy Savers (HER/HOMES + HEAR, $258.9M) NOT launched as of July 2026; DEP revising design to meet June 1, 2026 DOE guidance; both programs are low-to-moderate-income only, limiting relevance to a general residential track.

PPL $0.15/kWh custom and $0.20/kWh Direct Discount were fetched directly in July 2026 but the page states incentives 'may be terminated without prior notice', and no cost cap or pre-approval detail was published on that page.
states.notes_c: The PA 2026 TRM has a deemed Advanced Rooftop Controls measure (3.2.17), but it is strictly a DCV+economizer+fan-speed-reduction protocol on single-zone packaged units with functioning economizers - a compressor-cycling optimizer does not match it and would need the custom track, where PPL's $0.15/kWh is the standout rate. Small C&I HVAC tune-up (up to 20 tons, certified tech, no tune-up in prior 3 years, no maintenance contract) and refrigerant charge correction are deemed measures that may partially fit the CryogenX4 sales motion, but an additive itself is not a TRM measure. High-efficiency unitary/RTU replacement is classic deemed. Mid-2026 is a Phase IV to Phase V transition period: many program pages, catalogs, and rate sheets are being reissued.
states.notes_r: Rebate amounts are modest; Duquesne's residential rebate site says the program is 'currently being refreshed' and FirstEnergy's portal still showed Phase IV only in July 2026 - two of four major territories effectively dark for residential HVAC rebates at the moment.

d.model: competitive solicitation — CSPs are non-utility entities ("no direct/indirect ownership, partnership or affiliated interest with an EDC") that EDCs select and register to design/administer/manage EE&C plans
d.recipient: unknown — CSPs are compensated per their individual EDC contracts, not publicly standardized; portfolio-level EDC performance targets exist but per-project CSP payment structure not confirmed

d.enroll: Register as (or subcontract under) an EDC's registered Conservation Service Provider — CSP registration is required for entities providing consultation/design/admin/advisory services, but NOT required for entities that limit their role to installing measures or supplying equipment/materials

d.status: Genuine partial/adjacent match: Act 129 uses real, PUC-registered non-utility CSPs (a third-party-implementer structure) and calculates custom-project savings at the meter, but I could not confirm CSP compensation is tied to ongoing measured/NMEC savings (vs. a fixed program-delivery contract) — this is the key open question that determines whether PA is a true archetype D match.
d.notes: Flagged by the coordinator specifically ("Act 129 Phase V CSP structure") as a priority; recorded as pilot/partial rather than yes because CSP compensation mechanics (measured-savings-based vs. fixed-fee) could not be confirmed from public PUC materials reached this session — needs a follow-up reading of a specific EDC's CSP contract or Phase V implementation order.

states.apply_c: Online-portal, utility-by-utility applications: APS via the DNV-run S4B online application (Pre-Application required for Custom/ARC/EMS), SRP via savewithsrpbiz.com (Standard = post-install submission with invoices; Custom = written preapproval before purchase), TEP/UniSource via approved Trade Ally with mandatory pre-approval on all projects. No statewide administrator - three separate program relationships needed.
states.apply_r: Contractor-centric: TEP Efficient Home rebates are instant discounts taken off the invoice by participating (Trade Ally) contractors; SRP Cool Cash is a per-ton rebate application tied to qualifying contractor installs; IRA HEAR ('Efficiency Arizona') flows through qualified contractors statewide.
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive: SRP ARC controls $250/ton, unitary HP $110-135/ton; TEP $15-40/ton unitary. Custom: APS $0.02/kWh annual + $0.18/kWh summer on-peak up to 75% of cost; SRP $0.08/kWh + $300/avg peak kW up to 75% of incremental cost; TEP custom capped at 50% of incremental cost.
states.rebate_r: SRP Cool Cash $75/$150/$225 per ton by compressor type, up to $1,125; TEP up to $600 AC / $720 heat pump install, up to $160 AC tune-up, up to $100/ton mini-splits; HEAR up to $14,000 per household (income-qualified) incl. heat pump HVAC
states.pay: TEP: check within 6 weeks of final approval. SRP/APS: not published; APS pays only 'when funding is available' and currently has an Existing Facilities waitlist.
states.ira: HEAR is LIVE as 'Efficiency Arizona' (Governor's Office of Resiliency, ~$153M, runs through Sep 30, 2031 or fund exhaustion) but uptake is slow - only ~800 rebates issued statewide as of March 2026. HOMES has NOT launched as of mid-2026 (multifamily expansion 'coming months'). Federal 25C/25D tax credits repealed effective Dec 31, 2025.
flags: APS Existing Facilities commercial rebate funding is EXHAUSTED (waitlist) as of mid-2026 - only ARC and School rebates funded; timing of FY2027 budget refresh needs confirmation with DNV program team

ACC voted Sept 2025 to begin repealing Arizona's utility energy-efficiency standards; APS/TEP DSM budgets become voluntary/annually re-approved - multi-year stability of ACC-regulated programs (APS, TEP, UNS) is uncertain; SRP (board-governed, not ACC) is the most stable

states.notes_c: Advanced RTU controls is a first-class measure in AZ: SRP has it deemed at $250/ton and APS has a dedicated ARC program paying up to 100% of incremental cost (pilot scoped to schools/nonprofits - fit for general commercial needs confirmation). APS custom rate structure heavily rewards summer on-peak (3-8pm Jun-Sep) kWh - ideal for compressor-cycling savings if peak-period savings can be shown. CryogenX4 has no deemed path anywhere; APS/SRP custom both require pre/post verification and (APS) a Societal Cost Test. SRP is not ACC-regulated and self-funds its programs - most stable partner.

APS residential HVAC offerings not verified this pass - confirm current APS residential rebate status separately.

No fixed metering duration stated in the July 2026 Policies & Procedures.

programs.budget: Annual ACC-approved DSMAC budget; waitlist created when Final Applications total the annual budget. states.apply_c: Dominantly utility-run programs applied through online portals or utility reps with a registered Participating Contractor/Trade Ally: Con Edison's Incentive Navigator portal downstate, National Grid rep-driven applications upstate, NYSEG/RG&E via Franklin Energy trade allies, PSEG LI via Prime Efficiency Partners. Pre-approval (Notice to Proceed / pre-approved rebate) before installation is required essentially everywhere for custom, and at Con Edison for everything.
states.apply_r: Dominant design is NYS Clean Heat: heat-pump rebates administered by the seven sponsoring utilities (Central Hudson, Con Edison, National Fuel, National Grid, NYSEG, O&R, RG&E) and delivered through participating contractors, typically netted off the contractor's invoice; income-eligible households layer NYSERDA EmPower+ with federal HEAR funds.
states.trm: New York Standard Approach for Estimating Energy Savings (NY TRM) Version 13, effective January 1, 2026 (Record of Revision effective March 31, 2026)
states.rebate_c: Custom: $0.25/kWh saved capped at 65% of cost (National Grid UNY); Con Edison category custom rates $0.35-$0.85/kWh capped at 50% of project cost; PSEG LI custom capped at 70% of installed cost; prescriptive unitary HVAC ~$175-$300/ton (PSEG LI)
states.rebate_r: Third-party trackers report roughly $5,000-$12,000 for air-source heat pumps depending on utility territory, decommissioning, and DAC status; EmPower+ with HEAR up to $24,000 for income-qualifying households (NYSERDA)
states.ira: New York was the first state to launch IRA home energy rebates (June 2024). As of mid-2026 both are live: HEAR flows through NYSERDA's EmPower+ for income-eligible 1-4 unit homes; HOMES ($158M, modeled-savings whole-home design) launched with higher rebates for LMI households. Funds available until expended or Sep 30, 2031.
flags: Con Edison electric C&I eligibility requires >100 kW average peak demand and excludes multifamily - many small-RTU targets in NYC may be ineligible for the flagship program; verify whether a small-business pathway exists downstate.

NY TRM V13 full text not directly parsed; the Advanced Rooftop Control (ARC) measure was verified only via TRM stakeholder-forum references. Confirm whether the ARC characterization (which typically assumes supply-fan VFD + DCV/economizer) covers a compressor-cycling-only controller like HVAC OPTIMIZER.
NYSEG/RG&E custom $/kWh rate and payment timeline not found in fetched pages - the detailed 2026 rebate catalog PDFs failed to load; needs follow-up.

PSEG LI $0.16/kWh figure appears in the lighting section of the prescriptive guide; the general custom electric rate for HVAC custom projects was not separately documented (only the 70%-of-installed-cost cap, which came from search summary rather than a directly parsed program document).

Payment timelines are not published by any NY utility examined; Con Edison's 2025 closeout ran through December with post-inspections and final engineering reviews, suggesting multi-month application-to-check.
Residential ASHP rebate range ($5,000-$12,000) comes from third-party aggregator sites, not utility rate sheets; verify against each utility's NYS Clean Heat rebate table.
Statewide lighting sunset (Dec 31, 2025) signals active PSC restructuring of utility portfolios for the 2026-2030 cycle; HVAC/electrification budgets appear favored but program terms may shift.

No M&V metering durations (7-day vs 30-day) were stated in any fetched document; Con Edison requires an M&V plan for Neighborhood custom bonuses and clarified M&V timing in its 2026 manual - pull Section 4.0 of the Con Ed C&I Program Manual for specifics.
Central Hudson and Orange & Rockland were not profiled (smaller territories); add if Hudson Valley expansion matters.
states.notes_c: Con Edison C&I electric measures require accounts >100 kW average peak demand and exclude multifamily - a major constraint for small-RTU commercial customers in NYC. Con Edison 2026 application window is narrow (May 1-Sep 30) with install-by Oct 15. Statewide lighting incentives sunset Dec 31, 2025 per PSC directive, shifting budgets toward HVAC/electrification. Prescriptive path = NY TRM measures at Con Edison, so if HVAC OPTIMIZER maps to the TRM ARC measure it could go prescriptive; otherwise custom at $0.25-$0.35/kWh rates with utility engineering review.
states.notes_r: Residential rebates center on heat pumps/electrification, not AC efficiency add-ons - no visible residential path for a refrigerant additive or compressor-cycling controller. NYS Clean Heat requires the installer to be a program participating contractor.

d.programs: Business Energy Pro (BEP) — a NYSERDA/Con Edison Pay-for-Performance pilot (2019-2022, Staten Island and Westchester County); no confirmed active commercial successor as of 2026
d.admin: NYSERDA in partnership with Con Edison (utility)
d.model: historical: competitive solicitation — NYSERDA/Con Edison jointly issued an RFP selecting "Portfolio Managers" (aggregators/implementers), ~$10M available, 1-3 selected
d.recipient: aggregator (historical BEP pilot; Portfolio Managers paid on NMEC performance)
d.pay: historical: measured/metered NMEC savings (CalTRACK methodology via a NYSERDA-designated AMV Solution Provider), paid over time to Portfolio Managers
d.enroll: No open enrollment currently found; BEP was geographically limited (Staten Island, Westchester) and RFP-based, and appears discontinued. NYSERDA's current "Building Operations & Performance" page lists only the deemed/cost-share "On-site Energy Manager Program." Con Edison's 2025-2026 C&I Energy Efficiency & Building Electrification program materials (under a May 2025 PSC order authorizing ~$1.68B in EE/BE funding for 2026-2030) do not show explicit NMEC/P4P branding; Con Edison's separate Non-Wires Solutions program has Installation + Performance Payments but is a demand-response/non-wires-alternative structure, not a general commercial EE P4P track.
d.fit: optimizer and cryogenx4 would plausibly have fit BEP (NMEC is measure-agnostic); rtu_replacement and thermal_barrier also fit; solar_thermal likely fits if it reduces metered gas/electric load — but with no confirmed active successor, there is no current enrollment path for any measure
d.status: Business Energy Pro pilot concluded around 2022; despite direct searching (NYSERDA's own /bep page, current Building Operations & Performance page, Con Edison C&I materials), no active 2023-2026 statewide or utility-specific commercial successor was found.
d.notes: This is the closest confirmed historical match to archetype D in the Northeast, and the PSC's May 2025 order authorizing a large new 2026-2030 EE/BE portfolio for Con Edison is worth a dedicated follow-up to see whether any NMEC/P4P provisions were embedded in the new program design docs (not located in this pass).

states.trm: Connecticut Program Savings Document (PSD), 2026 edition (filed with DEEP 3/1/26 as part of the 2026 Update to the 2025-2027 C&LM Plan); 624 pages
states.rebate_c: Energy Opportunities custom: up to 40% of installed cost; SBEA: up to 80% of total project cost; commercial heat pump express: $250/ton (like-for-like ASHP) to $1,650-$4,000/ton (energy optimization), capped at 75% of installation cost
states.rebate_r: $250/ton up to $2,500 combined for qualifying air-source heat pumps (like-for-like/cooling-only track, offer window 1/1/26-12/31/26); higher amounts under the Residential Energy Optimization track when displacing fossil/electric-resistance heat (amount not captured from a fetched document)
states.ira: Not yet launched per CT DEEP's IRA Home Energy Rebate page as fetched July 2026: CT is allocated $49.73M HEAR and $49.83M HER; HEAR State Implementation Blueprints were submitted to DOE end of April 2025 and are listed as under DOE review, with HER blueprints in drafting; page still states hoped launch of HEAR 'mid-2025' and HER 'early 2026' contingent on DOE approval, suggesting the page may be stale and launch has slipped - verify current status directly with DEEP
flags: Payment timeline (application-to-check days) is not published in any document fetched; EO pays only after post-installation inspection and verification - speed score is conservative and should be validated with the utility account reps

No custom $/kWh incentive rate was found in fetched documents; CT's custom incentives are quoted as % of installed cost (40% EO / 80% SBEA) rather than a published $/kWh rate - a $/kWh schedule may exist in internal EO program materials not publicly posted

No PSD deemed measure specifically covers compressor-cycling RTU controllers (OPTIMIZER); closest is PSD 2.2.19 fan speed control and the EO 'occupancy-based HVAC controls'/EMS category - whether OPTIMIZER can ride a deemed category or must go custom needs a conversation with Eversource/UI program engineers

CryoGenX4 (refrigerant additive) has no deemed or named path anywhere in the 2026 PSD; only plausible route is PSD 2.8 Custom with engineering review and billing/metered calibration; no fixed metering duration (7-day vs 30-day) is specified in the PSD custom sections reviewed

CT DEEP's IRA page (fetched July 2026) still says HEAR launch hoped 'mid-2025' and is under DOE review - page appears stale and the actual mid-2026 launch status (including any federal funding disruption) needs direct confirmation with DEEP

Municipal utilities (CMEEC members: Norwich, Groton, Wallingford, etc.) are outside the Energize CT Energy Efficiency Fund and were not researched in depth; customers there are not eligible for the programs above
Rebate T&Cs explicitly state funding availability is not guaranteed; CT has a history of Energy Efficiency Fund budget pressure - stability score of 4 assumes the DEEP-approved 2025-2027 plan holds
Residential Energy Optimization (fossil-displacement) rebate amounts were not captured from a fetched document and are left out rather than estimated

energizect.com blocks generic fetchers (403); data was obtained via direct download with a browser user-agent - some program subpages (e.g. commercial ASHP express $250/ton detail page) render key details behind JavaScript, so the $250/ton commercial figure comes from the search-result snippet of the EnergizeCT page and its residential analog; verify on the live page
states.notes_c: Pre-approval thresholds on the express track are concrete: projects over 20 tons or over $30,000 in rebates require pre-approval and post-inspection (plus pre-approval for Eversource customers using third-party financing). EO custom requires a signed project agreement BEFORE ordering equipment and pays only after installation is inspected and verified. OPTIMIZER's closest deemed hook is PSD 2.2.19 (RTU fan speed control) and the EO controls/EMS category; a compressor-cycling device would most likely be run as an EO custom measure with engineering review. High-efficiency RTU/unitary replacement is a classic deemed path (PSD 2.2.2 plus HP express $/ton tiers with IEER/COP minimums).
states.notes_r: Projects are randomly selected for inspection. 0.99% Smart-E Loan financing promo for heat pumps through 7/31/26. Residential path is heat-pump-centric; no residential deemed measure found for aftermarket AC controls or refrigerant additives.

states.ira: Not yet launched as of mid-2026. Kansas Energy Office (Kansas Corporation Commission) says the Kansas Home Rebates Program is 'coming soon'; public application portal (kshomerebates.gov) not yet open; contractor recruitment underway at kshomerebates.gov/contractors. Third-party trackers report portals in final launch stages during 2026 with >$100M in federal funding, but the official KCC page confirms no open applications yet.
flags: CRITICAL for HVAC OPTIMIZER: Evergy custom rules require simple payback >= 12 months BEFORE incentive; a ~$400/unit controller with strong savings may pay back too fast to qualify - needs a call with the TRC outreach associate to confirm treatment (bundling with other measures may fix this).

CRYOGENX4: no explicit exclusion of refrigerant additives found, but the T&C exclusion of voltage-reduction/power-conditioning 'purporting' technologies signals skepticism toward non-standard measures; expect full custom scrutiny and possible rejection - not verified either way.
Custom M&V metering duration (7-day vs 30-day) is NOT published; T&C only say the program 'will specify period, frequency, and format' case by case.

The Evergy KEEIA TRM/Deemed Savings Table itself (filed at estar.kcc.ks.gov) was not directly inspected; whether an advanced-RTU-controls deemed measure exists inside it is unconfirmed - the public 2026 brochure shows none.
Pre-approval review turnaround time (application to Offer) is undocumented; only the post-completion 8-week payment target is stated.
Liberty Utilities (Empire District) serves a small southeast-Kansas territory; no Kansas commercial efficiency program was found for it, but absence was not exhaustively verified.

IRA HOMES/HEAR: official KCC page still says 'coming soon' with no launch date; third-party claims of 2026 portal launch and >$100M funding and $8,000 HEAR heat-pump rebates were NOT verified against official Kansas documents.

Kansas has no statutory EERS; KEEIA participation is voluntary and Evergy 'may change any Program requirements... at any time without notice' - first-come first-served funds could exhaust before Dec 31, 2027.
KC BPU (largest muni) has terminated its rebate programs - Wyandotte County commercial customers currently have no utility rebate path.
Residential HEAR rebate range and income limits quoted from third-party aggregators only (energyrebatecalculator.com, rebateatlas.org) - treat as unverified.
states.notes_c: Evergy KS is effectively the whole commercial opportunity in Kansas. Key friction points: ALL custom measures need pre-approval, must pass a benefit-cost test, and must have a >=12-month simple payback BEFORE incentive - very fast-payback measures (possibly the ~$400 Optimizer on a single RTU) could be DISQUALIFIED by the 12-month-minimum-payback rule; bundle units or pair with other measures to lengthen payback. CRYOGENX4 risk: T&C explicitly exclude 'technologies purporting to reduce electricity usage through a reduction of voltage or power conditioning'; a refrigerant additive is not named but will face similar novel-technology scrutiny and full custom calculations, with EM&V (trend data/data logging) at program-specified duration. Very-high-efficiency RTU replacement fits Custom Lite HVAC perfectly ($/ton per IEER point - an IEER 31 unit vs ~14 IEER baseline could stack many points) but Custom Lite HVAC always requires pre-approval with nameplate photos. Contractor shared-savings contracts get cost re-determined at 'reasonable retail cost' - relevant if Energy Plus uses shared-savings pricing.
states.notes_r: Residential rebates run under the same KEEIA Cycle I authorization through Dec 31, 2027 with per-measure maximum payouts for the term. Trade Ally registration with Evergy is the gate for contractor-submitted (and upfront/instant) rebates - Energy Plus should register. No residential deemed measure matches the Optimizer or CRYOGENX4; residential value is via equipment-replacement rebates and, once launched, HEAR heat-pump rebates (up to $8,000, <=150% AMI per third-party sources - unverified against official KS documents).

states.rebate_c: Custom: Consumers pays $0.10/kWh first-year savings capped at 50% of project cost; DTE custom capped at 75% of measure cost (rate unpublished); I&M (IN program) $0.07/kWh up to 75%. Prescriptive unitary AC/RTU paid $/ton with IEER tiers (exact $ in applications, not catalogs). Annual customer caps $2M electric at both DTE and Consumers.
states.rebate_r: DTE: central AC $100-$300 (15.2-18+ SEER2), cold-climate ASHP $900-$1,200, mini-split HP $700-$1,000, ASHP tune-up $75. Consumers: central AC $150-$300, ASHP $300, mini-split $350, GSHP $200-$300. MiHER (IRA): HEAR up to $14,000 income-qualified electrification, HOMES up to $8,000 whole-home.
states.pay: DTE: check 4-6 weeks after final approval; Consumers: 6-8 weeks after Final Application approval; plus upfront reservation/pre-approval cycle (DTE allows up to 14 days for pre-inspection) and 60-90 day project-completion windows.
states.ira: Live. Michigan Home Energy Rebates (MiHER), run by EGLE with CLEAResult as implementer, piloted Oct 2024 in the UP and launched statewide April 23, 2025; both HOMES and HEAR are accepting applications as of mid-2026 (~$105M HEAR allocation, ~$211M total MI Home Energy Rebates funding per EGLE/press materials).
flags: Neither DTE nor Consumers publishes prescriptive dollar amounts in the catalog - they live in the rebate APPLICATION worksheets. Exact $/ton for unitary AC and $/ton for tune-ups/controls measures need a pull of the DTE BusinessProgramRebateApplication.pdf and Consumers Incentive Application before quoting numbers to customers.
DTE's custom $/kWh rate is not published anywhere fetched - rebate is set during the reservation/CICP process. Do not assume a rate; only the 75%-of-measure-cost cap and >1yr payback are documented.

MEMD contents could not be directly inspected (not publicly searchable); 'advanced RTU controls' presence in MEMD is unverified. Utility catalogs strongly suggest no deemed pathway for compressor-cycling controllers.

Indiana Michigan Power's electricideas.com custom page is written for Indiana; I&M Michigan customers are listed under Efficiency United. Which program a MI I&M customer uses needs a phone confirmation.

Efficiency United C&I custom terms (third-party sources cite ~40% of cost up to $10,000 for MGU with mandatory pre-approval and 2-7 yr payback band) were NOT verified on a fetched primary page - confirm before relying on them.

MEMD/MiHER details (Integral Analytics maintenance, April 23 2025 statewide launch, $105M HEAR allocation, HEAR up to $14k / HOMES up to $8k) came from search-result summaries of michigan.gov pages rather than full page fetches - high plausibility but verify amounts on EGLE's MiHER page before customer-facing use.

Metering duration: Michigan customs are calc-based by default; the only explicit duration found is Consumers' 7 continuous days pre/post line-side metering for VFD customs (15-sec intervals). Both utilities reserve the right to require M&V case-by-case - no statewide 30-day rule found.

CryoGenX4 risk: both utilities exclude 'changes in operational/maintenance practices or simple control modifications not involving capital costs' and require savings from a system-efficiency improvement; a refrigerant additive will face skeptical engineering review and possibly required pre/post metering. No Michigan precedent found for additive approval.

Reservation/Pre-Notification BEFORE touching existing equipment is mandatory for custom at both IOUs (DTE: baseline must be verifiable while old equipment still operates). This constrains the retrofit sales process.
Program funds are limited/first-come at all four territories; DTE final apps due Nov 30, 2026 and I&M Dec 15, 2026 - Q4 project completions risk missing the program year.
states.notes_c: No Michigan utility catalog has a deemed advanced-RTU-controls (compressor-cycling) measure, so HVAC OPTIMIZER rides custom: Consumers explicitly allows automated control technology under custom (calc-based, metering at program discretion; 7-day pre/post line-side metering is the stated standard for VFD customs and a good proxy for what controls projects face). CryoGenX4 is problematic under both customs: DTE excludes 'simple control modifications not involving capital costs' but an additive should count as capital; expect full engineering scrutiny and possible required pre/post metering. High-efficiency RTU replacement is a classic deemed $/ton measure at both IOUs (DTE HE-2 to HE-6; Consumers HV101). RTU refrigerant-charge-correction tune-up (DTE HE-48, $/ton) is an interesting adjacent deemed measure for refrigerant-side work. Reservation BEFORE removing old equipment is mandatory for all custom work at both utilities - retrofit-first sales motions will forfeit rebates.
states.notes_r: Participating-contractor registration with each IOU is a hard gate - Consumers states non-participating contractor installs are ineligible. MiHER uses registered contractors as well. Compressor-cycling controls and refrigerant additives are not deemed residential measures at either IOU; the residential play is riding HVAC replacement/tune-up rebates.

states.apply_c: Everything runs through Efficiency Maine Trust statewide, regardless of utility. Prescriptive projects must go through an Efficiency Maine Qualified Partner (we would register as one) with pre-approval before equipment purchase; custom projects apply under the competitive PON-EM-001-2026 via a signed electronic cover sheet and application package to the Custom Program team.
states.apply_r: Statewide Efficiency Maine residential rebates require installation by an Efficiency Maine Residential Registered Vendor; the standard path is a mail-in/uploaded rebate claim form after installation (claim within 6 months), with ~6-week processing; some vendors deduct the rebate from the invoice and claim it themselves.
states.trm: Efficiency Maine Trust Technical Reference Manual â€” Commercial/Industrial/Multifamily TRM v2024.3 (226 pp.); separate Retail/Residential TRM (latest observed v2026.3)
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive HVAC examples: heat pump RTUs $28-$168/MBH, single-packaged heat pumps $2,200-$6,500/unit, VFDs $400-$2,300, VRF $3-$12/sq ft. Custom: $0.30/kWh annual savings up to 50% of net project cost, $5k-$1M per entity per fiscal year.
states.rebate_r: Whole-home heat pumps: $1,000/outdoor unit (any income, $3,000 lifetime cap), $2,000 (moderate income, $6,000 cap), $3,000 (low income, $9,000 cap)
states.pay: Custom <$200k pays in one lump after completion + post-installation inspection (duration not stated); prescriptive payment timeline not published.
states.ira: Maine allocated ~$72M IRA rebate funds administered by Efficiency Maine under Maine DOER. HEAR ($35.7M, Sec. 50122) is live but only partially: limited to income-eligible new-construction affordable multifamily and single-family manufactured (mobile) homes â€” standard single-family homeowners not eligible. HOMES/HER application was still pending with DOE as of mid-2025; no evidence found of a launched broad HOMES program by mid-2026.
flags: Advanced Rooftop Controls is in the Commercial TRM as a prescriptive measure but its definition requires a VFD modulating RTU supply-fan speed; HVAC OPTIMIZER (compressor cycling, no fan VFD) likely fails the measure spec â€” confirm with Efficiency Maine whether a compressor-cycling controller can qualify under ARC or must go Custom. Also, ARC did not appear on the current commercial HVAC incentives web page (which lists VFDs but not ARC), so verify the measure is actively offered with a published $ amount.

CRYOGENX4: Custom PON excludes measures relying solely on behavior or facility maintenance and gives the Trust sole discretion to reject; viability of a refrigerant additive under Custom is unverified.

Custom Program economics conflict with small-controller projects: $5,000-$10,000 minimum incentive and >1.0-year post-incentive simple payback requirement; $400/unit Optimizer deployments would need large portfolios and may fail the payback-floor test in reverse (payback must EXCEED 1 year after incentive).
No published metering-duration standard (7-day vs 30-day) found; PON says M&V terms are set per project by the Trust with independent third-party verification.
Prescriptive payment timeline (application-to-check) not published anywhere fetched; residential claims state ~6 weeks.

Current commercial prescriptive unitary offerings are heat-pump-centric; no cooling-only high-IEER RTU prescriptive category observed â€” the FUTURE IEER-31 RTU product may need to qualify as a heat pump RTU or go Custom.

CMP page (cmpco.com) timed out on fetch; the claim that CMP and Versant run no separate efficiency programs rests on Efficiency Maine's statewide-administrator role (statutory funding under 35-A MRSA Â§10110 cited in the PON) and third-party confirmations, not a fetched utility page.

Transmission/subtransmission-voltage customers are NOT eligible for the standard electric-efficiency-funded incentives (35-A MRSA Â§10110(6)); they fall back to RGGI funds when available â€” screen large industrial leads for service voltage.

IRA HOMES/HEAR status is based on search-result snippets of maine.gov and efficiencymaine.com (mid-2025 data): HEAR partial (multifamily new construction + manufactured homes only), HOMES pending DOE approval; confirm current mid-2026 status directly.
Commercial TRM v2024.3 was the latest commercial version found; a newer FY26 commercial TRM may exist (residential TRM is at v2026.3).
states.notes_c: The TRM's Advanced Rooftop Controls deemed measure requires a supply-fan VFD, so HVAC OPTIMIZER (compressor cycling on constant-speed units) likely cannot use it as-is and would need the Custom Program â€” which requires $5k-$10k minimum incentive, competitive application, independent engineering review, 50% customer cost share, and >1-year post-incentive payback. CRYOGENX4 faces an additional hurdle: the PON excludes measures 'that rely solely on human behavior changes or facility maintenance' and reserves the right to reject applications, so an additive would need to be framed as installed equipment/treatment with validated savings. Prescriptive high-efficiency unitary offerings are heat-pump-oriented (heat pump RTUs, packaged HPs); a cooling-only IEER-31 RTU category was not observed on the HVAC incentives page. All prescriptive HVAC requires pre-approval before purchase and a Qualified Partner (contractor registration: application, insurance certificate, training webinars).
states.notes_r: Rebate processing stated as ~6 weeks. Registered Vendor requirement is strict (rebate denied without one). Some vendors offer point-of-sale discounting, but the official program design is a post-installation claim form.

flags: Ameren Advanced RTU Controls deemed measure definition requires economizer + supply-fan VFD + DCV retrofit; the $400 compressor-cycling OPTIMIZER alone likely fails the deemed definition - confirm with BizSavers team whether it can qualify as standard or must go custom

Ameren custom $/kWh rate not published; only the 50%/100% caps are documented, and the fetched custom guidelines PDF is from the 2019-2022 cycle - current 2025-26 custom guidelines should be requested from BizSavers

Evergy T&Cs exclude 'voltage reduction or power conditioning' technologies; CRYOGENX4 will need clear engineering documentation to avoid being lumped into excluded exotic-technology category

Budget-exhaustion risk is real: Ameren's 2024 BizSavers budget was fully allocated mid-year (queue system), and Evergy MO eliminated all lighting incentives for Cycle IV; MEEIA is voluntary (no statutory EERS) and MEEA characterizes Cycle 4 as dis-investment
Evergy MO residential HVAC rebate chart fetched is the 2024 (MEEIA 3) version; whether broad residential HVAC rebates continue under Cycle IV 2025-26 is unverified
Ameren PAYS rebate table PDF has ambiguous column alignment (e.g., which measure gets $500/ton vs $2,000/system); confirm exact per-measure amounts before quoting customers
Liberty (Empire) and City Utilities of Springfield details are thin: rates, pre-approval, and payment timelines not published on fetched pages; DSIRE detail pages did not render

states.notes_c: Ameren's Advanced RTU Controls deemed measure requires economizer + supply-fan VFD + DCV, so the compressor-cycling-only OPTIMIZER likely rides custom unless bundled to meet the definition. Evergy T&Cs explicitly exclude 'technologies purporting to reduce electricity usage through a reduction of voltage or power conditioning' - CRYOGENX4 is refrigerant-side, not voltage, but expect heavy engineering scrutiny; custom requires pre-approval and Evergy can reject/modify savings claims. states.apply_c: In OPPD territory (Omaha metro, the biggest commercial market), Energy Plus would register as an OPPD Trade Ally and submit prescriptive ARC/HVAC rebates through OPPD's online application software (no preapproval under $5,000; preapproval above). In NPPD/EnergyWise territory it's simple PDF forms filed with the customer's local utility post-install; in Lincoln, a participating SEP contractor submits and the rebate lands as an invoice credit.
states.apply_r: Contractor-driven paper/online rebate applications: OPPD HVAC Smart rebates ($265-$525 by SEER tier, all heat pumps $525) are submitted by the licensed installing contractor with the customer receiving a check; EnergyWise utilities pay $400-$1,200 for air-source/mini-split heat pumps (geothermal $2,400-$3,300) via post-install forms filed with the local utility; LES/City of Lincoln stack up to ~$3,800 for heat pumps with the incentive credited on the participating contractor's invoice.
states.rebate_c: Prescriptive: OPPD RTUs $100-$200/ton, ARC controls $135-$207/ton, chillers $50-$300/ton; EnergyWise HVAC $30-$330/ton. Custom: OPPD $500/kW peak demand reduction up to 50% of project cost (max $100k); EnergyWise custom capped at 50% of cost. Equipment rebates at OPPD capped at 50% of material cost; $100k/facility/year.
states.rebate_r: $265-$1,200 for AC/heat pumps at OPPD and EnergyWise utilities; geothermal $2,400-$3,300 (EnergyWise); up to ~$3,800 stacked LES + City of Lincoln heat pump incentives; tune-up $30 (EnergyWise cooling tune-up); OPPD also offers an HVAC tune-up rebate
states.pay: Prescriptive: likely weeks (OPPD residential benchmark ~6 weeks; business not published - flag). OPPD custom: months - final payment only after the June-September billing season post-completion plus case-study approval, potentially 6-12+ months for a project finished in fall.
states.ira: Not launched as of mid-2026: Nebraska's ~$91M HOMES/HEAR allocation (administered by the NE Dept. of Water, Energy and Environment) remains in 'Preparing Application' status with DOE with no announced launch date
flags: LES commercial per-ton incentive amounts could not be verified: les.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, and the 2025/2026 commercial heat pump/AC PDF was unreadable; a human should pull the 'Commercial High-Efficiency Heat Pumps and Air Conditioners' PDF from les.com or email SEP@les.com.
OPPD business prescriptive payment timeline (days to check) is not published; the ~6-week figure is from OPPD's residential program and used only as a proxy.

OPPD ARC rebates are restricted to devices 'expressly shown on the application form' from an approved vendor list - HVAC OPTIMIZER must be added to OPPD's ARC approved list before the deemed path works; OPPD's T&C explicitly excludes ARC equipment from the custom pathway, so if the device is not listed there may be NO OPPD path. Confirm listing process with OPPD trade ally team.

OPPD custom rebates pay on peak kW demand reduction only ($500/kW), not $/kWh, and final payment waits for the June-September billing season post-completion - projects finished in autumn may wait ~a year for final payment (30% advance available at preapproval). Also custom and prescriptive rebates cannot be combined on the same building in the same calendar year.

CryogenX4: OPPD custom requires >=5% verified sustainable savings, an Energy Study, Trade Ally submission, and hot-weather sub-metering (min 3 weeks) or June-Sept bill comparison - viable but slow; no deemed path anywhere in NE.
EnergyWise 'HVAC System Optimization' program page content could not be retrieved (empty page); incentive calculation and M&V for that offering are unverified - contact NPPD EnergyWise consultant.
No metering-duration requirement was found in any EnergyWise document (custom incentives are set by utility Energy Efficiency Consultants case-by-case).

IRA HOMES/HEAR 'Preparing Application' status came from a third-party tracker (rebateatlas.org) plus NE DWEE program listings; given mid-2026 federal uncertainty around unobligated IRA funds, verify directly with the Nebraska Dept. of Water, Energy and Environment before citing to customers.

Nebraska has no EERS mandate; all programs are voluntary public-power budgets with first-come first-served exhaustion (OPPD documents an explicit SOLD OUT mechanism), so late-year project timing is a real risk.
Utility count/territory ranking (OPPD ~largest by customers, NPPD statewide G&T via retail utilities, LES ~Lincoln) was not re-verified with customer-count data this session.
states.notes_c: OPPD is the standout: ARC (advanced RTU controllers) is an explicit deemed measure at $135-$207/ton, but only devices expressly listed on the application form / approved vendor list qualify, ARC is one-to-one with the RTU, existing buildings only, and a 3-year RTU service agreement (ASHRAE/ACCA 180) is required - getting HVAC OPTIMIZER onto OPPD's approved ARC list is the critical GTM step, because OPPD's T&C explicitly bars ARC equipment from the custom pathway. CryogenX4 would ride OPPD custom ($500/kW, 5% minimum verified savings, PE/energy study, 3-weeks-of-hot-weather sub-metering or June-Sept bill comparison) or EnergyWise custom/industrial-process; refrigeration projects are an explicitly eligible OPPD custom category. Solar-thermal HVAC assist has no prescriptive slot and would also be custom. OPPD prohibits combining custom and prescriptive rebates on the same building in the same calendar year.
states.notes_r: OPPD requires application within the calendar year and within 4 months of install; qualifying heat pumps also unlock OPPD's lower winter conservation rate (Rate 115). EnergyWise pays contractors a $50 dealer incentive per qualified heat pump install. LES SEP funds are annual, first-come first-served. IRA rebates cannot yet be counted on in Nebraska sales motions.
